title: Balanced Signals
statement: An array contains only 0,1,2. Find the longest contiguous segment in which all three values occur equally often.
pivot: Represent each prefix by two independent count differences. Equal prefix states imply the intervening segment added equal amounts of all three values.

title: Target Sum Under a Length Contract
statement: Count contiguous subarrays with sum exactly K and length between L and R inclusive. Values may be negative.
pivot: For each right endpoint, only prefix indices aged L..R are legal partners. Add and expire prefix sums from a frequency map.

title: One Reorder, Best Gain
statement: Choose one contiguous subarray and sort only that subarray. Maximize the final array's maximum subarray sum.
pivot: Reason about which crossing prefix/suffix contributions sorting can improve; the entire array need not be recomputed for every interval.

title: Window With Two Budgets
statement: Find the longest subarray containing at most K distinct values and at most M values whose frequency inside the window is odd.
pivot: Track distinct count and an odd-frequency counter; both update in O(1) as elements enter or leave.

title: Shortest Heavy Segment
statement: Given signed integers, find the shortest non-empty contiguous subarray whose sum is at least S.
pivot: Negative values break ordinary sliding-window monotonicity. Maintain only prefix candidates that can still produce an optimal answer.

title: Minimum Cover With One Waiver
statement: Find the shortest substring of S containing all characters of T with multiplicity, except one required occurrence may be ignored.
pivot: Validity becomes total missing required occurrences ≤ 1, which remains incrementally maintainable while expanding and shrinking.

title: Factory Days
statement: Jobs must be processed in order. Each day handles one contiguous block, paying setup C plus block sum. Use at most D days and minimize the maximum daily total.
coverage: Binary search on answer / greedy feasibility
pivot: Guess a daily cap X. Feasibility is monotone; greedily pack the longest legal prefix into each day.

title: Two Sorted Logs, One Cut
statement: Two sorted arrays are given. Return the median of their union without merging them.
pivot: Search a cut in the smaller array so the combined left side has half the elements and every left value is ≤ every right value.

title: K-th Cross Distance
statement: Two sorted arrays A and B are given. Among all |A[i]-B[j]| values, return the k-th smallest.
coverage: Binary search on value + pair counting
pivot: Binary-search a distance d and count cross-array pairs within d using moving boundaries in sorted order.

title: Bounded Subarray Minimum Sum
statement: Compute the sum of the minimum element over every contiguous subarray whose length is at most K.
pivot: Assign each subarray to a unique minimum index, then count only left/right extent pairs whose combined length respects K.

title: Circular Greater Within Deadline
statement: For each index i, return the first strictly greater value seen moving forward circularly, but inspect at most K subsequent positions.
pivot: Process a doubled stream while unresolved indices expire after K steps.

title: Histogram After One Removal
statement: Remove at most one histogram bar completely, closing the gap, then return the largest rectangle area.
pivot: A deletion can merge regions separated by one obstruction. Derive contributions from nearest-smaller boundaries instead of trying every deletion naively.

title: Intersection With Cycles
statement: Two singly linked lists may each contain a cycle. Return a shared node if they intersect, otherwise null.
pivot: Classify both lists by cycle entry; acyclic/acyclic, mixed, and cyclic/cyclic cases have different invariants.

title: Conditional Group Reversal
statement: Traverse a linked list in groups of sizes 1,2,3,... Reverse a group only if its full length exists and its group size is prime.
pivot: Separate discovering the exact group boundary from reversing it; never mutate before confirming the full group.

title: Median With Erase
statement: Maintain a multiset supporting insert(x), erase(x), and median(). Erase may target values buried inside your data structure.
pivot: Use two heaps with logical sizes and delayed-deletion counters; prune stale tops before balancing or reading the median.

title: K-th Largest Pair Sum
statement: Arrays A and B are sorted descending. Return the k-th largest A[i]+B[j] without generating all pairs.
coverage: Heap / best-first search on monotone matrix
pivot: Treat index pairs as a monotone grid. Start at (0,0), pop the best state, and push unseen neighboring states.

title: Mandatory Meeting
statement: Select the maximum number of non-overlapping meetings, but one specified meeting must be included.
pivot: Condition on the mandatory interval; the remaining choice separates into independent before and after scheduling problems.

title: Minimum Refuels With Restricted Stops
statement: Reach distance T using stations with position and fuel. You may refuel at at most K stations, taking all fuel there. Minimize refuels or report impossible.
pivot: When fuel runs out, retroactively choose the largest fuel among passed stations; exchange reasoning shows this is safe.

title: Wildcard Word Trace
statement: Trace word W through adjacent grid cells without reuse. Once, one chosen grid cell may match any required character.
pivot: Add one bit for whether the wildcard has been consumed, and backtrack visited state precisely.

title: Queens With Holes
statement: Count N-Queens placements when some board cells are forbidden.
pivot: Search row by row; forbidden cells affect candidates while columns and diagonals remain the sufficient conflict state.

title: Distance K From Many Sources
statement: Given a binary tree, target nodes, forbidden nodes, and K, return legal nodes whose shortest tree distance from any target is exactly K. Paths cannot cross forbidden nodes.
pivot: Add parent links, view the tree as an undirected graph, and launch one BFS from all legal targets.

title: Maximum Tree Path With One Zero
statement: In a weighted binary tree, choose any simple path. You may replace at most one node value on that path by 0. Maximize path sum.
pivot: Each node needs downward-path states for privilege unused and already used; combine child states carefully through the node.

title: BST Rank Outside a Forbidden Band
statement: A balanced BST stores subtree sizes. Query(L,R,k) asks for the k-th smallest key not in [L,R].
pivot: Use ranks to count the lower block and the excluded band, then translate the requested outside rank into a global rank.

title: Rechargeable Wall-Break BFS
statement: In a grid, entering a wall consumes one of K charges; recharge cells restore charges to K. Find the shortest path from start to goal.
pivot: Position alone is not the state; remaining charges change future reachability.

title: Flight With Stops and One Discount
statement: Find minimum cost from s to t using at most K edges. Once, one chosen edge may be paid at floor(cost/2).
pivot: Future possibilities depend on node, steps used, and whether the discount is consumed; encode all three in the state.

title: Delete One Prerequisite
statement: A directed graph may contain cycles. Return one edge whose deletion makes it acyclic, or report impossible if no single deletion suffices.
pivot: Find one directed cycle first. Any successful deleted edge must lie on that cycle, so only those candidates need testing.

title: Threshold Connectivity
statement: For many queries (u,v,T), determine whether u and v are connected using only edges of weight at most T.
pivot: Sort edges and queries by threshold, adding edges to DSU as each query threshold becomes active.

title: Second-Best Network
statement: Given a connected weighted undirected graph, find the weight of the minimum spanning tree strictly heavier than the MST.
pivot: Build one MST; every alternative adds one non-tree edge and removes the maximum-weight edge on the created cycle.

title: SCC Source Count After One New Edge
statement: Given a directed graph, you may add one edge anywhere. What is the minimum number of starting vertices needed so every vertex becomes reachable from at least one start?
pivot: Compress SCCs. The answer depends on source components in the condensation DAG and how one added edge can reduce that count.

title: Circular Robber With Exact Count
statement: Houses lie in a circle. Choose exactly K non-adjacent houses maximizing total value; values may be negative.
coverage: DP with count dimension / circular split
pivot: Break the first-last dependency into cases and add chosen-count as a DP dimension.

title: Nested Envelopes With Equal-Width Traps
statement: Given envelopes (w,h), find the longest strict nesting chain where both width and height must increase.
pivot: Sort width ascending and height descending for equal widths, then compute LIS on heights to prevent illegal equal-width nesting.

title: Last Removal Wins
statement: Repeatedly remove one interior weight x and score leftNeighbor*x*rightNeighbor; outside endpoints behave as 1. Maximize total score.
pivot: Choose which item is removed last inside an interval; at that moment its surviving neighbors are exactly the interval boundaries.

title: Edit Distance With One Free Deletion Block
statement: Transform A into B with unit insert/delete/replace costs. Once, delete one contiguous positive-length block from A for total cost 0.
pivot: Add a phase: free block not started, currently deleting for free, or already finished.

title: Constrained Word Break
statement: Segment S into dictionary words, but consecutive chosen words may not begin with the same character. Determine if a valid segmentation exists.
pivot: Ordinary word-break state is insufficient; retain the previous word's first character while a trie enumerates legal next words.

title: Dynamic Prefix Rank
statement: Maintain an array under point updates. Query(l,r,x) asks how many values in A[l..r] are ≤ x.
pivot: The query has both index and value dimensions. Build a tree over one dimension whose nodes summarize the other.

title: Balanced Window With a Cost Cap
statement: Find the longest subarray where counts of 0,1,2 differ by at most one and total element cost is at most B.
pivot: One constraint is monotone under shrinking while balance is relative-count state; find a representation that lets both coexist.

title: Capacity With Mandatory Breaks
statement: Split ordered jobs across at most D days. Each day has setup C, and every M jobs globally incur break cost R in the containing day. Minimize maximum daily time.
pivot: Binary-search the cap, but the greedy feasibility checker must account for global break boundaries incrementally.

title: Median After Excluding a Value Band
statement: Two sorted arrays and interval [L,R] are given. Return the median of all elements outside [L,R] without materializing filtered arrays.
pivot: Combine selection with fast counts of legal values ≤ candidate; exclusion changes ranks but not sortedness.

title: Nested Boxes With One Repair
statement: Boxes have width and height. Increase either dimension of at most one box by 1 before choosing a strict nesting chain. Maximize chain length.
pivot: Treat the repaired box as a bridge between a best compatible prefix chain and suffix chain using LIS/order summaries.

title: Tree Path With Exactly K Marked Nodes
statement: In a weighted tree, find the maximum-sum simple path containing exactly K marked vertices.
pivot: Each subtree exports best downward paths indexed by marked-count; combining children is a small knapsack convolution.

title: Grid Escape With Keys, Breaks, and Recharges
statement: Find the shortest grid path with doors requiring keys, walls consuming break charges, and recharge cells restoring charges. Keys are permanent.
pivot: The real state is position, key mask, and remaining charges; dominance can prune strictly worse states.

title: Cheapest Route With Time Windows
statement: Edges have cost and travel time; each vertex is enterable only during specified time windows. Reach t within total time T at minimum cost.
pivot: Cost-optimal arrival depends on vertex and elapsed time; use a layered state graph or DP-style relaxation over time.

title: Build Order With Expiring Priorities
statement: Tasks form a DAG with priority and deadline position. Produce a topological order minimizing tasks placed after deadline; break ties by higher priority.
pivot: Kahn's algorithm gives the frontier; the real optimization is which currently available task to schedule next and why that local rule is safe.

title: Threshold Connectivity With Component Scores
statement: Weighted edges activate as threshold T rises. Each vertex has a score. Query(u,T) asks for the maximum score in u's component using edges ≤ T.
pivot: Sort by threshold; DSU components maintain aggregate maxima as edges activate.

title: Dictionary Segmentation With Patterned Pieces
statement: Segment S into dictionary words. Segment j must also match pattern phase P[j mod m]. Minimize number of segments.
pivot: DP state includes string position and pattern phase; trie traversal enumerates dictionary matches while phase filters admissibility.

title: Maximum Valid Subarray Under Two Extremes
statement: Find the longest subarray with max-min ≤ D and sum at least S; values may be negative.
pivot: Max/min is maintained by deques while signed-sum feasibility needs prefix-order reasoning; synchronize the two sets of feasible left endpoints.

title: First Prefix Reaching a Dynamic Target
statement: Maintain a nonnegative array under point updates. Query(l,T) asks for the smallest r≥l with sum(A[l..r]) ≥ T.
pivot: Store segment sums and descend the tree, subtracting whole covered segments until the first threshold crossing is located.

title: Meeting Rooms With Cancellation Budget
statement: Given intervals, R identical rooms, and at most K cancellations, maximize the number of meetings hosted.
pivot: Sweep by start time. When overlap exceeds capacity, identify which active meeting is best to discard, usually the one blocking a room longest.

title: Perfect Assignment With Forbidden Pairs
statement: Assign n workers to n jobs at minimum total cost. Some pairs are forbidden, and exactly K workers must receive jobs from a special subset.
pivot: Memoize by used-job mask and special-count; worker index is implied by number of assigned jobs.

title: Shortest Safe Route With One Teleport
statement: A directed graph has travel time and risk on edges. Find minimum-time s→t path with total risk ≤ R. Once, teleport between equal-label vertices at zero time but fixed risk C.
coverage: Graph search × multiple constraints × implicit edges
pivot: Expand state by accumulated risk and teleport-used bit; process same-label teleport groups without materializing quadratic edges.
